name: Question 14
problem: Given that $g\cdot h=8$, find the angle between $g=⟨t,t,t-1⟩$ and $h=⟨4,-2,-1⟩.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
First, since $g\cdot h=8$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}g\cdot h & =8 \\ t\cdot 4+t\cdot (-2)+(t-1)\cdot (-1) & =8 \\ 4t-2t-t+1 & =8 \\ t+1 & =8 \\ t & =7\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}g & =⟨7,7,7-1⟩ \\  & =⟨7,7,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $g$ and $h$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{g\cdot h}{|\,g\,||\,h\,|} \\  & =\frac{{g}_{x}{h}_{x}+{g}_{y}{h}_{y}+{g}_{z}{h}_{z}}{\sqrt{{g}_{x}^{2}+{g}_{y}^{2}+{g}_{z}^{2}}\sqrt{{h}_{x}^{2}+{h}_{y}^{2}+{h}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{{7}^{2}+{7}^{2}+{6}^{2}}\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{134}\cdot \sqrt{21}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{2\,814}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{8}{\sqrt{2\,814}})≈{81.33}^{∘}.
$$

Question 14
?

Given that g⋅h=8, find the angle between g=⟨t,t,t−1⟩ and h=⟨4,−2,−1⟩. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

a
87.33∘
b
72.34∘
c
88.21∘
d
81.33∘
e
67.13∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, since g⋅h=8, we can solve for t, as follows:

g⋅h=8t⋅4+t⋅(−2)+(t−1)⋅(−1)=84t−2t−t+1=8t+1=8t=7

So, g=⟨7,7,7−1⟩=⟨7,7,6⟩.

Now, the cosine of the angle between g and h is

cos⁡θ=g⋅h|g||h|=gxhx+gyhy+gzhzgx2+gy2+gz2hx2+hy2+hz2=872+72+6242+(−2)2+(−1)2=8134⋅21=82814.

Therefore, θ=arccos⁡(82814)≈81.33∘.
